title: Normalized coherent scalar is compatible with inverse-image composition
statement: Let j:Y to X, b:Z to Y and k:Z to X be etale morphisms with k=b followed by j. Let G be quasi-coherent on X, with quasi-coherent tensor pullbacks, and r a global function on Y. Define restrictionScalar(j,G,r) on j inverse image of the lifted coherent sheaf by conjugating the coefficient map induced by multiplication by r on j tensor pullback G through coherentEtaleRestrictionIso(j,G). Then the inverse image along b of restrictionScalar(j,G,r), followed by the inverse of upperStarComp(b,j,k), equals that inverse followed by restrictionScalar(k,G,b.appTop r). Dependencies: [def-weil-pbc-restriction-scalar-endomorphism].

source.place: Tag 03Q8, lemma-higher-direct-images, restriction of cohomology classes; Descent Tag 03DR, tensor-section restriction.

proof.text:
identify each etale inverse image with localization restriction. The chosen
coherent restriction isomorphism has component the inverse tensor-composition
isomorphism. Conjugating multiplication through it is multiplication by the scalar
restricted to each etale test scheme, since tensor-composition maps are module-linear.
The comparison of inverse-image composition with localization restriction composition
is upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction_comp. Its localization component restricts
along the mapComp isomorphism of test objects, whose underlying scheme map is the
identity. The semilinearity equation etaleTensorSectionsRestriction_smul therefore
identifies the two scalar endomorphisms. Cancel the localization and composition
isomorphisms. All equalities also hold for zero modules, empty schemes, identity
morphisms, and the zero or unit scalar. This is a sheaf-level coefficient assertion;
it contains neither raw higher-image classes nor any cohomological degree.
